messages:
Maya: Quick sync — proposing a 3‑phase pilot for the Optimize toolkit (batching + caching + quant recommendation + eval-triggered alerts). TL;DR: discovery -> canary -> scale. Need alignment on acceptance criteria and what we gate in canary. https://redwood.ai/pilot-plan :point_right:
Jordan: +1. Can we call out SLO targets up front? p50/p95 latency, cost delta, and allowed quality regression. Otherwise engineers won't know what to optimize to.
Sanjay: From runtime side: prefer to land adaptive batching & prefix/KV caching on Dedicated first (predictable capacity) — hosted can follow. Main deps: KV cache API, routing fallback for quantized variants.
Lee: Ops note: must have telemetry, rollback hooks, and a clear incident playbook for canary. Eval-triggered alerts need to map to customer cohorts and alert severity.
Alex: Draft acceptance criteria suggestion (proposal):
- Latency: p95 increase <= 15% vs baseline for batched requests
- Cost: per-token/op cost reduction >= 10% for targeted workloads
- Quality: eval concordance drop <= 2% on our regression suite
- Reliability: no production error spike > 0.5% during canary
If we hit all four, we graduate to scale. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
Sanjay: That looks reasonable. Also require KV cache invalidation strategy (TTL + explicit invalidation) — otherwise customers will see stale completions.
Jordan: On quantization phasing: start with INT8 on non-critical models and compare outputs via the eval harness. If concordance < 98% then hold. Who owns the eval runs?
Alex: I can own weekly eval runs and produce a short report (diffs, examples, metric regressions). Will add a small pipeline job to run quant vs fp16 on canonical prompts.
Maya: Customer tranche proposal: AcmeHealth (high SLO), EduLab (medium), Chatly (low). Canary traffic split 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 2 weeks if no alerts.
Lee: Add a clear automatic rollback threshold: if eval-alert severity >= P2 or user-facing error rate > 0.5% for 5min, rollback to previous runner automatically. Ops will implement the circuit.
Sanjay: Quick config sketch for reference:
```
batching:
  max_batch_size: 128
  max_latency_ms: 15
cache:
  kv_ttl_ms: 300000
  explicit_invalidate: true
quant:
  enabled: false # flip in canary
```
Jordan: We also need cost monitoring per-route and token-level breakdown in Console for the pilot customers. Product: can you list the routes we enable?
Maya: Route list for canary (minimal): /v1/generate (short), /v1/chat (medium), /v1/embeddings (no quant). We'll lock embeddings out of quant for now.
Alex: Will add the acceptance gate checklist to the pilot doc and schedule weekly syncs. I'll run the eval job on Monday mornings.
ops-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: 2026-06-15T09:00Z -> canary slot created (id: canary-2876).
Lee: One more ask — retention window for eval traces = 30 days and we need a safe-mode toggle to disable batching per-customer.
Maya: OK — next steps: Alex to own eval gating, Sanjay to implement KV invalidation + config, Lee to add rollback/circuit plan, Jordan to define the exact metric dashboards, and I'll reach out to the three pilot customers for onboarding timeline. Aim to start discovery next Monday and run a 2‑week canary after that. Agree?
Jordan: Agree.
Sanjay: 👍
Lee: 👍
Alex: 👍 I'll post the checklist in the doc and tag owners.
Maya: Thanks all — I'll update the pilot-plan link with these items and ping for approvals. :rocket:
